html:
Rómulo Betancourt was a Venezuelan politician, founder of the Democratic Action party and president from 1945 to 1948 and from 1959 to 1964. He is called the father of Venezuelan democracy.

As a student he was jailed for protesting against Gómez in 1928. He founded Democratic Action in 1941, came to power in a coup in 1945, and brought in elections with universal suffrage. The army removed his party in 1948, and he spent ten years in exile under the dictator Marcos Pérez Jiménez.

After Pérez Jiménez fell in January 1958, the main parties signed the Punto Fijo Pact to share power and defend democracy. Betancourt was elected president, survived an assassination attempt by the Dominican dictator Trujillo, and handed power to an elected successor. The system lasted until the Caracazo and the rise of Chávez in Venezuela.
